answer: Each identity claims one knoll station on a voyage lane and locks a 70-credit bond. It files a key-signed sighting of a vessel leaving the wharf, with mark and time. An auditor checks the wharf departure log against the knoll sighting log; a mismatch, a reused sighting, or a second claim on the same knoll burns the bond. The first claim pays 36; the kth pays 36+8(k-1), so the 1000th pays 8028 and 1000 fakes pay 4,032,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-lookout ring fails because the auditor's logs decide, and one key holds one station. An honest agent locks 70 once and pays 36 once.
